items.passage: Who teaches scales on a bridge in February? He stopped me at every sour interval. He would tap the parapet twice, and I would begin again while barges slid underneath and my fingers went white. On the last of those Thursdays he set a coin on the stone and walked off without collecting it. Then he was gone: no letter, no forwarding address, eleven years. When he reappeared one spring, he gave no account of where he had been. I was teaching by then, and on a cold Thursday I had brought my own pupil to the same bridge, telling her that a room would only flatter her. Budi stood a little way off and listened through two scales. He did not tap the parapet once. When we finished, he nodded at my pupil, then at me, and went to buy chestnuts.
